label: Store a customer and their tier's latest
description: Data graph behind customer.register: the customer is stored and the latest registration of their tier is written beside it, and the graph answers only when both are in. The two writes move together -- a reader asking who was registered into gold most recently can never be told a customer that was not stored, and no customer can be stored without their tier's latest catching up. That is what atomic buys here, and it is one word rather than a graph that undoes what it wrote. The same graph as @customers/data/store-and-latest.graph.json, against the store kept in PostgreSQL: a store is named statically at a call site, so pointing these at another connection is a copy until a profile may swap one.

nodes.label: Write the customer under that key
Record it as the tier's latest
nodes.description: One row per tier, so a put under the tier replaces whatever was there.

nodes.label: Were both written, or did a constraint stop the customer?
A customer already uses this address
nodes.description: The store honoured a constraint it declares -- unique [email] -- and answered violated rather than writing. That is a conflict with what is kept, not a fault of the store, so it is refused as one; the transaction rolls back, and the latest row this run would have replaced is left as it was.

nodes.label: Nothing was written
nodes.description: The store answered neither a record nor a violated constraint, which no engine promises to do; the transaction rolls back, so neither write survives this refusal.

in.message: the store answered no record for {{in.email}}
